- When sentiment is consistently low or negative (0.00–0.20), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.00), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 2–5% downward correction to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is high (0.60+), model frequently overestimates; apply a 1–4% downward bias to align with mean reversion.  
- Model underestimates prices during early periods of strong downward sentiment; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–2% if sentiment drops below 0.20.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if recent 5-day average is >10% above 30-day average, reduce forecast by 1–3% to reflect reversion.  
- When sentiment is flat (0.00–0.20) and price is falling, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% to anticipate reversal.
